title: World Report 2022: Democratic Republic of Congo
claim: HRW says journalists, activists, whistleblowers, and critics of government policy were intimidated, threatened, beaten, arrested, and in some cases prosecuted by authorities and security forces; it also says supporters of Tshisekedi's UDPS attacked Catholic churches and priests over an independent electoral-commission push.
locator: Freedom of Expression, Peaceful Assembly, and Media section; 2021 background retained in 2022 report
source_confidence_reason: Independent rights report tying repression and party-aligned intimidation to the ruling environment.
period_fit: Transition into 2022 and inherited political-environment baseline
ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi's political environment and party ecosystem, but not every incident is a direct presidential order.
contrary_evidence: The same report also notes a transitional-justice commission and limited accountability steps in 2021-2022.

title: DR Congo: Martial Law Brings Crackdown in East
claim: HRW says the military and police curtailed freedom of expression, used lethal force against peaceful demonstrations, and arbitrarily detained and prosecuted activists, journalists, and political opposition members under martial law in North Kivu and Ituri.
source_confidence_reason: Detailed independent investigation with direct attribution to the martial-law governance structure under Tshisekedi.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant because Tshisekedi's administration maintained the state of siege and set its duration.
contrary_evidence: HRW notes the government justified martial law as an anti-insecurity measure and the report is focused on abuse allegations.

title: RDC: Kabund arrêté pour 'outrage au chef de l’État, imputations dommageables et diffamation'
claim: The AFP/Actualite report says Kabund was arrested in Kinshasa and charged with outrage against the head of state, harmful imputations, and defamation after he publicly denounced Tshisekedi's camp and launched his own party.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous wire-report corroboration with the charge language and political context spelled out.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Tshisekedi's political-space record.
contrary_evidence: The article also records criticism that the arrest could compromise free and credible 2023 elections.

title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation and the Second Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for the Democratic Republic of the Congo
claim: The IMF said the authorities had adopted prudent macroeconomic policies, most visibly by halting central bank financing to the government.
source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF press release with explicit policy attribution and date.
ruler_attribution: High: this describes the national authorities under Tshisekedi's government.
contrary_evidence: The same release says poverty remained very high and domestic arrears accumulated.

title: IMF Staff Completes 2022 Article IV and Program Review Mission to the Democratic Republic of the Congo
claim: IMF staff said sustaining reform efforts to improve public finance management, the business climate and governance remained critical to promote inclusive growth.
source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF mission statement from 2022 with direct reform assessment.
ruler_attribution: High: the mission assessed the incumbent government's policy agenda.
contrary_evidence: The same statement says the economy still faced spillovers from the war in Ukraine.

title: World Bank Supports the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Efforts to Improve Public Resources Management and Service Delivery
claim: The World Bank approved a project to increase mining revenue transparency and strengthen expenditure management at the central level and in selected provinces so that more funds reach public service delivery.
source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank project announcement with direct fiscal-governance objective.
period_fit: Pre-2022 reform baseline for the target year.
ruler_attribution: High: this is a government-supported reform package in the Tshisekedi period.
contrary_evidence: The project was approved because the underlying revenue and expenditure systems still needed strengthening.

title: World Bank Supports the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Efforts to Improve Public Resources Management and Service Delivery
claim: The project would support a single treasury account, better budget control, improved annual reporting, stronger oversight by the Court of Accounts, and enhanced civil-society participation in budgeting.
source_confidence_reason: Primary project design statement with concrete institutional reforms.
ruler_attribution: High: the reforms are tied to the incumbent government's public financial management agenda.
contrary_evidence: The statement itself implies the reforms were still needed, so this is not evidence of success by itself.

title: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has achieved a high overall score in implementing the 2019 EITI Standard
claim: The EITI Board commended the DRC for the timeliness of its disclosures and its thematic reports on SOEs, licensing, contract disclosure, beneficial ownership, subnational transfers, mining royalties, and barter-type infrastructure provisions.
source_confidence_reason: Independent international validation of disclosure practices.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: strong institutional transparency evidence, but not a direct measure of household welfare.
contrary_evidence: The same decision says beneficial ownership and some newer standards were not yet fully implemented.

title: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has achieved a high overall score in implementing the 2019 EITI Standard
claim: The EITI Secretariat said the DRC had only partly met the beneficial-ownership objective and that only 21 of 77 significant extractive licensees submitted beneficial-ownership information in the cited report period.
source_confidence_reason: Independent validation report with a concrete quantitative gap.
ruler_attribution: High: this is about extractive-sector transparency under the incumbent government.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes some progress in open-format disclosure.

title: Top Congo presidential adviser resigns after allegedly requesting bribe on tape
claim: Reuters reported that a top adviser to President Felix Tshisekedi resigned after being caught on tape allegedly negotiating a corrupt mineral deal.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a concrete corruption scandal involving a presidential adviser.
ruler_attribution: High: the adviser was a close figure in Tshisekedi's current cabinet and election network.
contrary_evidence: The adviser denied wrongdoing and the presidency said violators would suffer consequences.

title: I Will Take My Percentage: Congolese Presidential Adviser Caught on Tape Negotiating Corrupt Mineral Deal
claim: OCCRP said the adviser described his closeness to President Felix Tshisekedi and was recorded offering access to mining licenses in exchange for a stake in a joint venture.
source_confidence_reason: Primary investigative reporting with direct recording-based allegations.
ruler_attribution: High: the conduct was tied to a close presidential adviser invoking access to Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: The recording appears to be an apparent sting operation, so the evidentiary chain should be kept explicit.

title: Child Labor and Human Rights Violations in the Mining Industry of the Democratic Republic of Congo
claim: HRW said Tshisekedi's administration had made many promises of reform but little action, and that corrupt and abusive practices and repression against journalists, activists, critics, and peaceful protesters had continued or escalated.
source_confidence_reason: Direct testimony from a major rights NGO grounded in contemporaneous reporting.
period_fit: Direct 2022 target-period governance and welfare evidence.
ruler_attribution: High: the statement explicitly assesses Tshisekedi's administration.
contrary_evidence: The same testimony notes some positive early steps such as releasing political prisoners.

title: Child Labor and Human Rights Violations in the Mining Industry of the Democratic Republic of Congo
claim: HRW said an activist died after denouncing embezzlement of mining royalties and that police violently dispersed an opposition sit-in over the election law, injuring and arresting protesters.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous human-rights testimony with specific incident detail.
period_fit: Direct 2022 target-period evidence on corruption and coercive response.
ruler_attribution: High: the incidents are attributed to state actors under the incumbent administration.
contrary_evidence: The report also shows the government remained under domestic and international pressure to reform.

title: DR Congo: State Mining Company Subject to a Damning Audit
claim: OCCRP reports that the anti-corruption agency found severe irregularities, including embezzlement, at state mining company Gecamines that deprived the state budget of hundreds of millions of dollars.
source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting on an audit by the anti-corruption agency; the finding is attributed to the audit and is specific, though the article is reporting rather than the audit text itself.
period_fit: 2022; directly relevant to Tshisekedi-era governance and mining-sector integrity
ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful: the audit concerns a state enterprise under Tshisekedi's government, not a personal act by Tshisekedi himself.
contrary_evidence: The article does not prove personal enrichment by Tshisekedi or his family.
It is an audit-based allegation rather than a court finding in the article itself.

title: DR Congo: State Mining Company Subject to a Damning Audit
claim: The same OCCRP report says the audit was commissioned in September 2021 by President Felix Tshisekedi, who had pledged to scrutinize and renegotiate mining agreements closed under his predecessor.
locator: paragraph beginning 'The audit was commissioned in September last year'
source_confidence_reason: Direct statement of a presidential action reported by OCCRP; the commissioning is specific and ruler-attributable, though the article is secondary reporting.
period_fit: retrospective but relevant to 2022 because it shows an anti-corruption oversight step taken by Tshisekedi before and during the target year
ruler_attribution: Direct: Tshisekedi is named as the commissioner of the audit.
contrary_evidence: Commissioning an audit does not show the audit was effective.
The article also reports severe corruption at the enterprise, limiting the strength of the positive inference.

title: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has achieved a high overall score in implementing the 2019 EITI Standard
claim: EITI says that in the 2018-2020 reporting cycle only 21 of 77 extractive licensees with significant revenues submitted beneficial ownership information, and that the legal framework for beneficial ownership disclosures was still incomplete.
source_confidence_reason: Independent international transparency body, specific numerical disclosure gap, and a clear locator in the validation decision.
period_fit: 2022; the validation decision evaluates disclosure practices that were current in the target-period governance environment
ruler_attribution: Indirect: this is sector transparency under Tshisekedi's government rather than a personal act, but it reflects the integrity environment around extractive governance.
contrary_evidence: The same decision notes the DRC achieved a high overall score on implementation.
This does not by itself show Tshisekedi personally concealed ownership or profited.

title: Des proches de Tshisekedi accusés de corruption
claim: DW reports that several close associates of Tshisekedi were accused of corruption or embezzlement, and that Tshisekedi had not yet reacted to these cases at the time of publication.
source_confidence_reason: The article is a reputable international outlet summarizing multiple named corruption allegations, but it remains a secondary report over a cluster of cases involving associates rather than Tshisekedi personally.
period_fit: 2022; directly within the target year and about Tshisekedi's governing circle
ruler_attribution: Indirect: the allegations concern close associates, ministers, and party figures in Tshisekedi's orbit; no direct proof of Tshisekedi's personal knowledge or benefit is supplied here.
contrary_evidence: The article does not establish Tshisekedi's personal participation in the alleged corruption.
Some named figures were later acquitted or denied wrongdoing.

title: DR Congo: No Inquiry into Police Role in Ethnic Killings
claim: HRW says Congolese authorities had not meaningfully investigated police involvement in the Buhene killings, and that after martial law came into force President Tshisekedi appointed the police commander in charge of the attacks as deputy territory administrator.
source_confidence_reason: HRW gives a dated, specific account with named officials and a clear attribution chain to the president's appointment decision.
period_fit: 2022, with retrospective reference to April 2021 events that shaped 2022 accountability choices
ruler_attribution: Direct for the appointment and indirect for the failure to investigate; the article ties both to Tshisekedi-era authorities.
contrary_evidence: The underlying violence began in 2021, so the failure is partly inherited.
The article does not prove Tshisekedi personally ordered the non-investigation.

title: RDC : Félix Tshisekedi encourage le gouvernement à récupérer le patrimoine immobilier de l’État acquis indûment par des tiers
claim: Radio Okapi reports that Tshisekedi urged the government to recover state real estate acquired unlawfully by third parties and to ensure transparency and respect for the law.
locator: paragraph beginning 'Le Président Félix Antoine Tshisekedi a encouragé...'
source_confidence_reason: The report quotes a specific presidential instruction from a mainstream Congolese outlet, but it is still official rhetoric rather than proof of execution.
period_fit: 2022; direct ruler statement during the target year
ruler_attribution: Direct: the quotation is attributed to Tshisekedi at a cabinet meeting.
contrary_evidence: This is a promise or instruction, not proof of implementation.
The report does not show whether the recovery campaign succeeded or was selective.

title: "I Will Take My Percentage": Congolese Presidential Adviser Caught on Tape Negotiating Corrupt Mineral Deal
claim: A covert-recording investigation showed Vidiye Tshimanga, one of Tshisekedi's closest advisers, offering to help investors win mining licenses and cut red tape in exchange for a stake, while describing ways to hide his share through proxies and offshore trusts.
source_confidence_reason: The claim is supported by direct recordings, named participants, and in-article confirmation that the meetings occurred.
period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target period and tied to Tshisekedi's inner-circle network.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the conduct is by a close presidential adviser using proximity to Tshisekedi and claiming access through him.
contrary_evidence: Tshimanga denied wrongdoing and said the statements were taken out of context

title: Top Congo presidential adviser resigns after allegedly requesting bribe on tape
claim: Reuters reported that Tshimanga resigned after being caught on tape negotiating a corrupt mineral deal, and that Tshisekedi's communications director said the fight against corruption is one of the president's pillars and that anyone in the Office of the President who violated the law would suffer the consequences.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous wire reporting with a direct presidency response and no dependence on a single anonymous source family.
ruler_attribution: Direct to the president's office response; the underlying misconduct is by a close adviser in Tshisekedi's cabinet.

title: RDC : ouverture d'une information judiciaire à l'encontre de Vidiye Tshimanga

source_confidence_reason: Local outlet reporting a formal prosecutorial step in direct response to the recorded allegations.
ruler_attribution: Strong on the office network: the inquiry targeted a former special adviser to Tshisekedi, not an abstract national corruption climate.
contrary_evidence: The article reports allegations before final judgment

title: Que retenir de la nomination des nouveaux mandataires publics en RDC ?
claim: Ebuteli argued that Tshisekedi's September 2022 public-enterprise appointments kept a patronage pattern alive, with managers often chosen for party membership or family/friend ties and some appointees lacking sector experience.
source_confidence_reason: Independent Congolese research analysis that ties the appointments to a named ruling coalition and to specific selection criteria concerns, while remaining interpretive.
ruler_attribution: Direct to Tshisekedi's appointment power and coalition-management choices.
contrary_evidence: This is an analytic podcast, not an audit of every appointee

title: RDC : de nouvelles nominations à la tête des établissements publics

source_confidence_reason: Direct appointment notice with a detailed list of named appointees and office roles.
ruler_attribution: Direct: these were presidential appointments under Tshisekedi's formal authority.

title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo
claim: The State Department reported that in June Tshisekedi dismissed several Supreme Audit Court magistrates for failing to pursue corruption cases and appointed new leadership, then swore in 57 magistrates in August; it also said the APLC operated under the Office of the President.

ruler_attribution: Direct to Tshisekedi's authority over key accountability institutions.

title: RDC : l'APLC annonce avoir saisi une trentaine de camions des minerais et permis le recouvrement fiscal de plusieurs millions de USD dans le Lualaba au premier semestre 2022

source_confidence_reason: Specific operational claim from the presidential anti-corruption agency, but still self-reported and not independently audited in the article.
ruler_attribution: Moderate to strong: the APLC is a presidential anti-corruption service operating under Tshisekedi's office.
